newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Indian rebels threaten Bangladesh port - officials.
newsitem.headline: Indian rebels threaten Bangladesh port - officials.

text.p: Bangladesh authorities have tightened security at Chittagong port after suspected rebels from northeastern India threatened to blow it up, port officials said on Friday.

Zahiruddin Mahmood, chairman of the port, said he had received a mailed leaflet on Wednesday containing threats to blow up the port if Bangladesh joined an operation with India against insurgents in its northeastern states.
The threat came after Dhaka and New Delhi agreed recently to work together to contain insurgencies along their borders.
Officials of both countries have met twice in recent weeks in the Indian capital to discuss ways to combat the rebels.

Port officials said the leaflet was signed P.K. Barua and claimed to represent the views of the North Eastern Liberation Tigers (NELT), a combined force of guerrilla groups operating in India's seven northeastern states bordering Bangladesh.
They said the leaflet had been mailed from a post office in Chittagong.
Mahmood said he had conveyed the threat to intelligence agencies and tightened security in and around the port, which handles more than 80 percent of Bangladesh's foreign trade.
"We are not taking the threat as merely a joke. We have alerted our own security personnel... This port is very strategic for Bangladesh," one port official told Reuters.
He said the leaflet claimed the NELT had already deployed a group armed with dynamite and timebombs to target important government installations in Chittagong.
"The targets would be hit one after another if Bangladesh launched a joint operation against Indian tribal guerrillas or permits a corridor to India," the port official quoted the leaflet as saying.
The leaflet said the NELT had been trained by Tamil guerrillas in Sri Lanka.
